rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should explore a promising multimodal configuration. This experiment tests a multimodal model with multiprofile, PCA_n2000 RNA encoder, ImageNet ViT-L image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. It balances standard encoders and fusion strategies to establish a baseline for further exploration.

The existing evidence shows config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves 0.635 accuracy. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion, which are key differentiators from config_002. These changes address uncertainty about whether advanced encoders and attention-based methods could improve performance, balancing exploration of promising multimodal configurations with exploitation of the multiprofile setting.

The existing evidence shows config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.635). This experiment tests changing the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer while keeping other parameters the same, which could reveal if transformer aggregation improves performance. This balances exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation method) that may significantly impact results.

The existing evidence shows config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) has the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scvi_n200 while keeping other components identical, to determine if this change improves performance. It directly explores a key design choice (RNA encoder) in the current best configuration, balancing exploitation of the promising multimodal/multiprofile setup with exploration of alternative encoders.

The existing evidence shows config_036 (validation accuracy 0.706) is the top performer using pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 (config_038), a critical design choice that could improve performance. It balances exploitation (building on successful components) and exploration (testing alternative image encoders), prioritizing uncertainty reduction about the image encoder's impact on accuracy.

Existing evidence shows config_036 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping other components identical, to determine if this could further improve performance. It clarifies whether the aggregation method is a critical factor, leveraging the strong evidence from config_036.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (as in config_035) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (a simpler model) could maintain or improve performance, clarifying the impact of image encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the top-performing architecture with exploration of alternative components.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_035) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion to explore if combining these components could yield higher accuracy. It balances exploitation of proven aggregation/fusion strategies with exploration of RNA/image encoder combinations that may improve performance.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_035) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests a similar setup with resnet50 image encoder and concat fusion, clarifying whether the choice of image encoder or fusion method is critical. It balances exploration by testing a promising parameter combination while leveraging prior success with scvi_n200 and transformer.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (config_035: 0.724989). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, clarifying whether fusion method impacts performance. It's the best use of the final experiment to explore a critical design choice with high potential for improving accuracy.
